title: Summer picnics at the lake camps, prices and Lent
summary: Camps along the lake each had a band for Sunday picnics, paying seven dollars, with cheap whiskey and rent; Lent was slack.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: What happened during the summertime back then? They had many jobs for the music?

Oh yeah, on the picnic all night, on our Spanish folk. See, they had camps sitting over the water like you see some of them. They had them all the way out from Little Woods all the way to West End to Bucktown. Good. Them camps sitting on the water.

And every Sunday they'd play picnics from ten to six. Mm-hmm. They'd be playing Buddy Petit, Sam Morgan, oh man. Every camp would have a band. Every camp had a band. Man, now them jobs pay seven dollars, you work from ten to six. Mm.
Wasn't that a lot of money? Half a pint of whiskey, twenty-five cents. Six bits of a dollar a quarter. Yeah. Bare nickel a bottle. Sure. You could do a whole lot with that money. Mm-hmm.
Yes, indeed. House rent was cheap.

Our houses, anyhow, six dollars a month, seven dollars a month, two of them in the kitchen. But no convenience, you know, see. No water, nothing, no. And cisterns, you know, a yard, yeah. No convenience. Well, what about Lent? Did you have many jobs doing that?
No, during Lent we didn't have many.
Things would kind of slack off a little. But you had them dance at them halls. They'd still run. Oh.
Yeah, they would run. But the Catholic people, they would. .
